Three types of states based on attitude to religion – Atheistic State, Theocratic State, Secular State
Atheistic State – anti-religion, condemns all religions
Theocratic State – pro-religion, declares one particular religion as state religion (e.g., Bangladesh, Burma, Sri Lanka, Pakistan)
Secular State – neutral in matter of religion, does not uphold any particular religion (e.g., USA, India)

Democratic – polity based on doctrine of popular sovereignty
Doctrine of popular sovereignty – possession of supreme power by the people
Two types of democracy – direct and indirect
Direct democracy – people exercise supreme power directly (e.g., Switzerland)
Four devices of direct democracy – Referendum, Initiative, Recall, Plebiscite
Referendum – proposed legislation referred to electorate for direct vote
Initiative – people can propose a bill to legislature for enactment
Recall – voters can remove a representative or officer before expiry of term for failure to discharge duties
Plebiscite – method of obtaining opinion of people on any public issue, generally used for territorial disputes
Indirect democracy – representatives elected by people exercise supreme power
Indirect democracy also known as representative democracy
Two kinds of indirect democracy – parliamentary and presidential
Indian Constitution provides for representative parliamentary democracy
Executive responsible to legislature for all policies and actions
Universal adult franchise
Periodic elections
Rule of law
Independence of judiciary
Absence of discrimination on certain grounds – manifestations of democratic character

Republic – head of state always elected directly or indirectly for fixed period (e.g., USA)

Absence of any privileged class; all public offices open to every citizen without discrimination
Justice – three distinct forms: social, economic and political
Secured through Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles
Social justice – equal treatment of all citizens without social distinction (caste, colour, race, religion, sex)
Absence of privileges being extended to any particular section
Improvement in conditions of backward classes (SCs, STs and OBCs) and women
Economic justice – non-discrimination based on economic factors; elimination of glaring inequalities in wealth, income and property
Distributive justice – combination of social justice and economic justice
Political justice – equal political rights, equal access to political offices, equal voice in government

Article 326 – Elections to Lok Sabha and state assemblies on basis of adult suffrage
